paper.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
paper.central_claim: SayCan grounds the rich semantic knowledge of a large language model in learned robotic affordances, enabling a mobile manipulator to execute temporally extended abstract natural-language instructions in a real kitchen, with substantially higher performance than ungrounded baselines.
paper.central_claim_son55_wording: Pretrained skills with learned affordance (value) functions can ground an LLM planner: scoring each skill's language label under the LLM and multiplying by the skill's success probability lets a mobile manipulator execute long-horizon abstract instructions; reported 84% plan / 74% execution success over 101 instructions in a mock kitchen (81%/60% in a real kitchen), nearly doubling non-grounded baselines.

claims.text: SayCan grounds the rich semantic knowledge of a large language model in learned robotic affordances, enabling a mobile manipulator to execute temporally extended abstract natural-language instructions in a real kitchen, with substantially higher performance than ungrounded baselines.
claims.setting: PaLM540B; Everyday Robots mobile manipulator;15 objects,5 locations;101 instructions over7 families.
claims.baseline/control: No-VF67% planning; generative74% planning; their execution outcomes not supplied. FLAN70%/61% versus PaLM84%/74%.
claims.selection_vs_test: Prompt optimized with illustrative instruction simulator; models graduate through real kitchen skill evaluation.
claims.result/denominator: Mock84% planning/74% execution; real81%/60%; family results and101 instruction task list, not full per-task repeated outcomes.
claims.counterevidence: Abstract/introduction claim 'nearly doubles the performance over the non-grounded baselines' is contradicted by Table 2 totals: plan success 84% vs No VF 67% (1.25x) and Generative 74% (1.14x); only the 11-instruction Embodiment family approaches or exceeds doubling (64% vs 18%, ~3.6x; vs 36%, ~1.8x). No VF/Generative were not executed, so no execution-level grounding comparison exists; the no-LLM BC baselines (0%/9% execution) are not 'non-grounded LLM' baselines. Human-majority criteria, single trial per instruction, privileged known object locations.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author reports counted physical execution for this kitchen skill library and gains in grounded planning; not general autonomous kitchen competence or cleanly doubled physical success.

claims.allowed_conclusion: A concrete state-dependent selection mechanism, with measurable but incomplete reliability.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop real-robot execution with per-family counts (101 single-trial instructions) judged by 2-of-3 human raters; mock kitchen is the training environment, real kitchen used in skill graduation, navigation uses known object locations; one embodiment. Not transfer (EVIDENCE rule 2; anchors precedent 1).
assessment.author_claim_kept: SayCan grounds the rich semantic knowledge of a large language model in learned robotic affordances, enabling a mobile manipulator to execute temporally extended abstract natural-language instructions in a real kitchen, with substantially higher performance than ungrounded baselines. Abstract adds: grounding 'nearly doubles the performance over the non-grounded baselines'.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On one mobile manipulator in an office-kitchen setup, value-function-weighted PaLM skill selection reaches 84% plan / 74% execution success (mock) and 81% / 60% (real kitchen) on 101 author-designed single-trial instructions; plan success exceeds No-VF (67%) and Generative (74%) variants. The doubling claim holds only within the Embodiment family at plan level; execution-level benefit of grounding is not measured.
unresolved: Execution-level gain of the value function
assessment.reproduction: Author-reported only; nothing run by us.

G.reason: Specific, important bottleneck (LLM plans ignore what this robot can do in this state) demonstrated by the paper's own controls (embodiment family 64% vs 18% plan success without value functions); the closest concurrent neighbour (Huang et al.) is re-implemented as the Generative baseline; lineage (language-conditioned BC/RL, TAMP) and residue (no failure-aware replanning, skill range, negation) are stated. Meets the G=4 anchor; sol's reservation concerned our access to predecessor source versions, not the paper's gap definition.

M.reason: Product of LLM usefulness and affordance with an explicit assumption (a failed skill makes zero progress) gives distinguishable predictions tested by No-VF/Generative; calibration constants are empirical, place/terminate affordances hand-set, independence/probability reading unvalidated. Both seats agree.

X.reason: Algorithm 1, prompt and affordance formulas are given and permissions disclosed, but calibration constants are 'determined empirically' without the data/procedure, a completed-skill cap sits outside Algorithm 1, and two of three skill families use heuristic affordances (go-to from assumed-known object locations with d_max=100 m, i.e. near-flat at kitchen scale; place fixed at 1.0). The value-function grounding operation is fully realised only for pick, so the operation chain as executed is not fully reconstructible from the stated method.

measurement.reason: Defined 2-of-3 human-rater criteria for plan and execution with family denominators, but one trial per instruction (family percentages are k/11 or k/15), no rater agreement statistics, and value-function ablations are plan-level only (anchors v2 single-trial cap). Both seats agree.

causality.reason: No-VF and Generative controls are plan-level only, so the execution-level benefit of affordance grounding is never measured; navigation uses assumed-known object locations (privileged channel, anchors precedent 1 -> causality deduction); PaLM vs FLAN confounds model family and data. The abstract's 'nearly doubles' is not supported by Table 2 totals. Anchor 2: key gain with an unseparated confound.

holdout.reason: Mock kitchen is the skills' training environment; real-kitchen skill evaluations graduate models into SayCan; prompts tuned on a language simulator; one embodiment; privileged known locations. Real kitchen shows a 14-point execution drop. Both seats agree.

statistics.reason: Single trial per instruction and no variance/CI, but family denominators are stated and failures are decomposed (65% LLM vs 35% affordance, early termination, negation). Anchors v2 caps at <=1 only when there is neither repetition nor failure decomposition; a stated decomposition keeps it at 2.
